title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time
abstract: arXiv:2610.18515v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. translated_title: 大语言模型如何评估人类时间价值的全球视角
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地充当个人助理的角色；然而，人们对它们如何在全球范围内捕捉国家层面的偏好知之甚少。鉴于“时间”是一个具有普遍性和代表性的概念，我们通过仅改变用户所在的国家，并测量LLM认为对于60分钟约会延误而言合适的补偿金额，来考察LLM的时间偏好。随后，我们将LLM的回答与购买力平价人均GDP（GDP_PPP）、平均收入以及一个基于文献的指数（耐心得分）进行比较。我们在193个国家和5个LLM上的实验结果表明，不同LLM对世界各地人们时间的评估方式存在显著差异，且在提示词变化下的稳健性水平也各不相同。LLM始终为欧洲用户推荐最高的补偿，但大多为非洲用户推荐最低的补偿。基于GDP_PPP，LLM低估了居住在亚洲和南美洲用户的时间价值。这些发现……
tldr: 本研究通过在193个国家、5个大语言模型上的实验揭示，LLM对用户时间价值的评估因国家而显著不同——始终为欧洲用户推荐最高补偿、多为非洲用户推荐最低补偿，并基于GDP_PPP低估了亚洲和南美用户的时间价值。
en_tdlr: This study reveals, across 193 countries and 5 LLMs, that LLMs value users' time differently by country—consistently recommending the highest compensation for Europe and mostly the lowest for Africa, while underestimating the time value of users in Asia and South America based on GDP_PPP.
